title: What to Stream This Week: Musafir Cafe, Con City, Adarsh Baal Vidyalaya and More OTT Releases
excerpt: Vikrant Massey leads a hill-town romance on Netflix, a Tamil family drama about a money-printing machine hits the platform, and Kay Kay Menon takes over a failing school on Prime Video.
body:
• Musafir Cafe, starring Vikrant Massey, premieres on Netflix on July 24 — an eight-episode romantic drama based on Divya Prakash Dubey's bestselling Hindi novel.
  • Con City, a Tamil family drama about a receipt printer that starts generating money, arrives on Netflix the same day with an 8.9 IMDB rating.
  • Adarsh Baal Vidyalaya with Kay Kay Menon launches on Prime Video, following a laid-back headmaster racing to fix a broken government school.
  • The week also brings Pallichattambi on SonyLIV, Stuart Fails to Save the Universe from The Big Bang Theory universe, and Bleach's new anime arc.

This week's OTT calendar is stacked with new Indian content across languages and genres, headlined by two Netflix originals and a Prime Video series that together offer something for romance fans, regional cinema enthusiasts, and comedy lovers alike. Here are the standout titles streaming from July 20 to 26.

Musafir Cafe — Netflix, July 24

The most anticipated Hindi-language release this week is Musafir Cafe, an eight-episode romantic drama starring Vikrant Massey as Chander, a software engineer who moves to the mountains to pursue writing and opens a cafe in Mussoorie. Based on Divya Prakash Dubey's popular Hindi novel of the same name, the series follows Chander across two timelines as he navigates love, loss, and second chances.

"Based on Divya Prakash Dubey's popular Hindi novel of the same name, the series follows Chander across two timelines as he navigates love, loss, and second chances."

Vedika Pinto plays Sudha, a spirited divorce lawyer who becomes Chander's first love before circumstances pull them apart. Years later, Mahima Makwana enters as Preeti, who walks into his life at the cafe — just before Sudha makes a return. Directed by Ruchir Arun (Little Things, Ghar Waapsi), the series also features Adil Hussain and Rajeev Siddhartha. It is jointly produced by Terribly Tiny Tales and Homemade Stories, the production company Massey has co-founded.

Con City — Netflix, July 24

Tamil cinema's latest high-concept family drama arrives on the same day. Con City follows a struggling family whose lives are turned upside down when a receipt printer starts generating real money after a lightning strike. What begins as a windfall spirals into public chaos when the neighbourhood discovers the money-making machine.

Directed by Harish Durairaj, the film stars Arjun Das and Anna Ben alongside comedy favourite Yogi Babu. Available in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, and Hindi, it has already drawn an 8.9 IMDB rating — unusually high for a streaming debut. The premise sits in a tradition of Tamil films that use an absurd hook to explore economic anxiety and community dynamics.

Adarsh Baal Vidyalaya — Prime Video, July 24

Kay Kay Menon takes the lead in this seven-episode comedy-drama set in a fictional government school on the outskirts of Delhi. Menon plays Gyaneshwar Tripathi, a laid-back headmaster who learns that the top ten principals with the best board results will win a government-sponsored training trip to Cambridge University — a prize that suddenly motivates him to overhaul the institution.

Directed by Himank Gaur and produced by Posham Pa Pictures, the series co-stars Archana Puran Singh, Naveen Kasturia, and Deven Bhojani. The writing team includes Biswapati Sarkar, known for his work on TVF shows.

Also Streaming This Week

Pallichattambi (SonyLIV, July 24) — Tovino Thomas leads this Malayalam thriller about a scheming small-town operator whose survival depends on extracting himself from the mess his own plans have created.

Stuart Fails to Save the Universe — The Big Bang Theory franchise expands with a new spinoff following the comic-book store owner Stuart, landing for fans of the sitcom universe.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War — The Calamity — The latest arc of the beloved anime series continues its adaptation of the manga's final saga.

The week's releases also include The Devil Wears Prada 2 for international audiences, making this one of the busiest OTT slates of the month across platforms.
